Projection predictive feature selection

Source: R/projpred-package.R
projpred-package.Rd

The R package projpred performs the projection predictive variable (or "feature") selection for various regression models. We recommend to read the README file (available with enhanced formatting online) and the main vignette (topic = "projpred", but also available online) before continuing here.

Terminology

Throughout the whole package documentation, we use the term "submodel" for all kinds of candidate models onto which the reference model is projected. For custom reference models, the candidate models don't need to be actual submodels of the reference model, but in any case (even for custom reference models), the candidate models are always actual submodels of the full formula used by the search procedure. In this regard, it is correct to speak of submodels, even in case of a custom reference model.

The following model type abbreviations will be used at multiple places throughout the documentation: GLM (generalized linear model), GLMM (generalized linear multilevel—or "mixed"—model), GAM (generalized additive model), and GAMM (generalized additive multilevel—or "mixed"—model). Note that the term "generalized" includes the Gaussian family as well.

Draw-wise divergence minimizers

For the projection of the reference model onto a submodel, projpred currently relies on the following functions as draw-wise divergence minimizers (in other words, these are the workhorse functions employed by projpred's internal default div_minimizer functions, see init_refmodel()):

  • Submodel without multilevel or additive terms:

    • For the traditional (or latent) projection (or the augmented-data projection in case of the binomial() or brms::bernoulli() family): An internal C++ function which basically serves the same purpose as lm() for the gaussian() family and glm() for all other families. For the negative binomial family, projpred alternates the fit of this function (with the shape fixed) with a Newton search for the shape. The returned object inherits from class subfit. Possible tuning parameters for this internal C++ function are: regul (amount of ridge regularization; default: 1e-4), thresh_conv (convergence threshold; default: 1e-7, but not used in case of the Gaussian family with identity link), qa_updates_max (maximum number of quadratic approximation updates; default: 100, but fixed to 1 in case of the Gaussian family with identity link), ls_iter_max (maximum number of line search iterations; default: 30, but fixed to 1 in case of the Gaussian family with identity link), normalize (single logical value indicating whether to scale the predictors internally with the returned regression coefficient estimates being back-adjusted appropriately; default: TRUE), beta0_init (single numeric value giving the starting value for the intercept at centered predictors; default: 0, but for the negative binomial family the link function of the weighted mean response, minus the weighted mean offset), and beta_init (numeric vector giving the starting values for the regression coefficients; default: vector of 0s).

    • For the augmented-data projection: MASS::polr() (the returned object inherits from class polr) for the brms::cumulative() family or rstanarm::stan_polr() fits, nnet::multinom() (the returned object inherits from class multinom) for the brms::categorical() family.

  • Submodel with multilevel but no additive terms:

    • For the traditional (or latent) projection (or the augmented-data projection in case of the binomial() or brms::bernoulli() family): lme4::lmer() (the returned object inherits from class lmerMod) for the gaussian() family, lme4::glmer() (the returned object inherits from class glmerMod) for all other families. Exception: for the binomial() family with the logit link and the poisson() family with the log link, if all group-level terms are random intercepts (1 | <group>), projpred uses its own fit (the returned object inherits from class projpred_mlvl). This fit minimizes the Laplace approximation of lme4::glmer() (with nAGQ = 1), without rounding non-integer responses. projpred uses lme4::glmer() instead if the fit does not converge, if the submodel formula has an offset term, if the submodel has a rank-deficient model matrix or more than 500 group levels in total, if ... contains arguments of lme4::glmer() (for example control or nAGQ), or if global option projpred.mlvl_laplace is FALSE. After a fit that does not converge, the lme4::glmer() fit is returned as class projpred_mlvl, too. as_glmerMod() converts an object of class projpred_mlvl to class glmerMod. For lme4::glmer(), projpred uses control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"), so both optimization stages use BOBYQA. A control argument in ... replaces this default in the first fit. After some lme4 errors, projpred refits with its own settings and ignores this control. lme4 versions before 2.1-1 evaluate the objective of lme4::glmer() for the binomial() and the poisson() family with rounding: they round non-integer binomial responses and weights, and the objective is infinite for non-integer Poisson responses (then the group-level standard deviations stay at their start values). With these lme4 versions, projpred passes a copy of these families with another name (ending in _projpred) and an aic function without rounding. The submodel fits then have this family name, so for example lme4::simulate.merMod() does not work for them.

    • For the augmented-data projection: ordinal::clmm() (the returned object inherits from class clmm) for the brms::cumulative() family, mclogit::mblogit() (the returned object inherits from class mmblogit) for the brms::categorical() family. Exception: for the brms::cumulative() family, if the only group-level term is a random intercept (1 | <group>), projpred uses its own fit (the returned object inherits from classes projpred_mlvl_cumul and projpred_mlvl). This fit minimizes the Laplace approximation that ordinal::clmm() uses, for the links of brms::cumulative() (logit, probit, probit_approx, cloglog, cauchit). projpred uses ordinal::clmm() instead if the fit does not converge, if the submodel formula has an offset term, if the submodel has a rank-deficient model matrix, if ... contains arguments of ordinal::clmm() or of its optimizers (for example method or control), or if global option projpred.mlvl_laplace is FALSE. After a fit that does not converge, the ordinal::clmm() fit is returned as class projpred_mlvl_cumul, too. For ordinal::clmm() with a single group-level term (1 | <group>), projpred uses method = "ucminf" and grad = "forward" (see ordinal::clmm.control()). If this fit fails or does not converge, projpred refits with the default settings of ordinal::clmm(). An argument method or control in ... replaces this default. For the cloglog and loglog links, projpred always uses useMatrix = TRUE (see ordinal::clmm.control()) and does not use ucminf(). The code of ordinal::clmm() for a single group-level term uses the other of these two links. For the brms::categorical() family, projpred only supports catCov = "free" (see mclogit::mblogit()).

  • Submodel without multilevel but additive terms: mgcv::gam() (the returned object inherits from class gam). projpred uses the default method of mgcv::gam(). For the poisson() family, the responses of the traditional projection are not integers. Then mgcv::gam() with method = "REML" or method = "ML" stops with an error. Such a method can come from ... or (mgcv >= 1.9-5) from global option mgcv.gam.method.

  • Submodel with multilevel and additive terms: gamm4::gamm4() (within projpred, the returned object inherits from class gamm4). For the binomial() and the poisson() family, projpred passes the same family as to lme4::glmer() (see above).

  • Offsets: the submodels are fitted with the offsets of the reference model to its predicted means with offsets (for the augmented-data projection, to its predicted probabilities with offsets). This minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence from the reference model. For the gaussian() family with the identity link and for the latent projection, the fit without offsets gives the same coefficients, so projpred omits the offsets there. All offsets must be finite.

Verbosity, messages, warnings, errors

Global option projpred.verbose may be used for specifying the value passed to argument verbose of project(), varsel(), and cv_varsel().

By default, projpred catches messages and warnings from the draw-wise divergence minimizers and throws their unique collection after performing all draw-wise divergence minimizations (i.e., draw-wise projections). This can be deactivated by setting global option projpred.warn_proj_drawwise to FALSE.

Furthermore, by default, projpred checks the convergence of the draw-wise divergence minimizers and throws a warning if any seem to have not converged. This warning is thrown after the warning message from global option projpred.warn_proj_drawwise (see above) and can be deactivated by setting global option projpred.check_convergence to FALSE.

Parallelization

projpred can run two kinds of computations in parallel: the fold-wise computations of cv_varsel() (the CV parallelization, activated via argument parallel of cv_varsel(), which in turn can be controlled via global option projpred.parallel_cv) and the projections of the single draws (or clusters) of the reference model onto a submodel (the projection parallelization, see below).

Both use the parallel workers of the current plan of the future package, e.g., future::plan(future.mirai::mirai_multisession, workers = 4) from the future.mirai package or future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4). In our experiments with 8 workers, the first parallel call with the workers of future.mirai was faster than with those of future::multisession, and the workers of future.mirai returned big results faster (see the projection parallelization below). So we recommend the workers of future.mirai. With the sequential plan of future (the default), a parallel run is not possible, so projpred then runs sequentially and throws a warning. The workers must be able to load the same projpred installation as the main R session; projpred checks this. (If the main R session uses projpred via pkgload::load_all() or devtools::load_all(), the workers need to load the same source directory in the same way.) The parallelization is not tested on Windows.

The projection parallelization is controlled by global option projpred.parallel_proj_trigger: the number of projected draws below which the projections of the draws are not run in parallel (even if parallel workers are set up). Such a "trigger" threshold exists because of the computational overhead of a parallelization. By default, the projection parallelization is turned off, which can also be achieved by supplying Inf (or NULL) to option projpred.parallel_proj_trigger. The projection parallelization is mainly useful for submodels with multilevel or additive terms: for most other submodels, projpred fits all projected draws in a single call, which does not run in parallel. It is useful for varsel(), project(), and cv_varsel() without fold-wise computations; with the CV parallelization, the workers do not run the projections of their folds in parallel. Note that the fitted submodel objects of multilevel and additive submodels are quite big, which—when running in parallel—may lead to excessive memory usage which in turn may crash the R session (on Unix systems, setting an appropriate memory limit via unix::rlimit_as() may avoid crashing the whole machine). The workers also need time to return these objects to the main R session: in our experiments with 16 workers of future::multisession, this took longer than a sequential run, whereas 16 workers of future.mirai gave a clear speedup. So for the projection parallelization, we recommend the workers of future.mirai.

In the fold-wise computations of cv_varsel(), each CV fold has its own random number stream (L'Ecuyer-CMRG), which projpred derives from the random number generator of the main R session, with and without the CV parallelization. So for a given seed, the results depend neither on argument parallel, nor on the number of workers, nor on the plan of the future package.

A function goes to a parallel worker with its enclosing environments up to, but not including, the global environment. So if a function of a custom reference model is defined in a script and uses other objects of the global environment, the workers need these objects. If the globals package is installed, projpred finds them from the code of such functions and sends them to the workers. This cannot find objects whose names the code creates at run time (e.g., with get()). Global option projpred.export_to_workers may be set to a character vector of names of such objects, to export them from the global environment to the parallel workers as well. Setting that option to FALSE turns off any export of objects of the global environment.

During parallelization (either of the projection or the CV), progression updates can be received via the progressr package, e.g., by calling progressr::handlers(global = TRUE) before running the projection or the CV in parallel. The projpred package also offers the global option projpred.use_progressr for controlling whether to use the progressr package (TRUE or FALSE), but since that global option defaults to requireNamespace("progressr", quietly = TRUE) && interactive(), it usually does not need to be set by the user. Messages and warnings from the workers are shown in the main R session.

Monotonic terms

Global option projpred.mo_monotone (default TRUE) controls whether the projected effects of monotonic terms mo() are monotonic. See section "Monotonic terms" in init_refmodel() and mo_effects().

Multilevel models: "Integrating out" group-level effects

In case of multilevel models, projpred offers two global options for "integrating out" group-level effects: projpred.mlvl_pred_new and projpred.mlvl_proj_ref_new. When setting projpred.mlvl_pred_new to TRUE (default is FALSE), then at prediction time, projpred will treat group levels existing in the training data as new group levels, implying that their group-level effects are drawn randomly from a (multivariate) Gaussian distribution. This concerns both, the reference model and the (i.e., any) submodel. Furthermore, setting projpred.mlvl_pred_new to TRUE causes as.matrix.projection() and as_draws_matrix.projection() to omit the projected group-level effects (for the group levels from the original dataset). When setting projpred.mlvl_proj_ref_new to TRUE (default is FALSE), then at projection time, the reference model's fitted values (that the submodels fit to) will be computed by treating the group levels from the original dataset as new group levels, implying that their group-level effects will be drawn randomly from a (multivariate) Gaussian distribution (as long as the reference model is a multilevel model, which—for custom reference models—does not need to be the case). This also affects the latent response values for a latent projection correspondingly. Setting projpred.mlvl_pred_new to TRUE makes sense, e.g., when the prediction task is such that any group level will be treated as a new one. Typically, setting projpred.mlvl_proj_ref_new to TRUE only makes sense when projpred.mlvl_pred_new is already set to TRUE. In that case, the default of FALSE for projpred.mlvl_proj_ref_new ensures that at projection time, the submodels fit to the best possible fitted values from the reference model, and setting projpred.mlvl_proj_ref_new to TRUE would make sense if the group-level effects should be integrated out completely.

Memory usage

By setting the global option projpred.run_gc to TRUE, projpred will call gc() at some places (e.g., after each size that the forward search passes through) to free up some memory. These gc() calls are not always necessary to reduce the peak memory usage, but they add runtime (hence the default of FALSE for that global option).

During a call of varsel(), cv_varsel() or project(), projpred caches the submodel formulas and model matrices per set of predictor terms (for submodels without multilevel or additive terms). Global option projpred.proj_cache_mb (default 512) limits the size of this cache, in units of 2^20 bytes as estimated by utils::object.size(). The cache holds at most about twice this limit. The limit applies to each R process, so forked parallel workers can each have a cache of this size. Setting global option projpred.proj_cache to FALSE switches the cache off. The cache changes only the runtime, not the results.

Other notes

Global option projpred.digits controls arguments digits of print.vselsummary() and print.vsel().

There are several global options to control arguments of plot.vsel() and plot.cv_proportions() globally, see section "Usage" of the help pages of these two functions.

Global option projpred.warn_L1_interactions may be set to FALSE to deactivate a warning that an L1 search selected an interaction term before all involved lower-order interaction terms (including main-effect terms) were selected (in which case the predictor ranking is automatically modified by projpred so that the lower-order interaction terms come before this interaction term).

Most examples are not executed when called via example(). To execute them, their code has to be copied and pasted manually to the console.

Functions

init_refmodel(), get_refmodel()

For setting up an object containing information about the reference model, the submodels, and how the projection should be carried out. Explicit calls to init_refmodel() and get_refmodel() are only rarely needed.

varsel(), cv_varsel()

For running the search part and the evaluation part for a projection predictive variable selection, possibly with cross-validation (CV).

summary.vsel(), print.vsel(), plot.vsel(), suggest_size.vsel(), ranking(), cv_proportions(), plot.cv_proportions(), performances()

For post-processing the results from varsel() and cv_varsel().

project()

For projecting the reference model onto submodel(s). Typically, this follows the variable selection, but it can also be applied directly (without a variable selection).

as.matrix.projection() and as_draws_matrix.projection()

For extracting projected parameter draws.

proj_linpred(), proj_predict()

For making predictions from a submodel (after projecting the reference model onto it).
